subject: mathematics_2b
question_text: Find k if the pair of circles x² + y² − 5x − 14y − 34 = 0, x² + y² + 2x + 4y + k = 0 are orthogonal.

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: Write g, f, c for both circles
steps.margin_note: First mark. Both circles already have coefficient 1 on x² and y² — no dividing needed.
lines: From the given circles, we get
steps.why: Reading g, f, c off each circle (half the x-coefficient, half the y-coefficient, the constant term) is the setup step every orthogonality question needs before the condition can be applied.
common_mistakes: Reading g as −5 instead of −5/2 — it is HALF the coefficient of x, not the coefficient itself.
Mixing up which circle's values are primed and which are not.
steps.memory_tip: g and f are always half the coefficient of x and y — c is the constant term with no halving.

steps.label: Apply the orthogonal condition
steps.margin_note: Second mark, for solving the one linear equation in k.
steps.why: Two circles cut orthogonally exactly when 2gg′ + 2ff′ = c + c′ — substituting the known g, f, c values leaves one linear equation in the single unknown k.
common_mistakes: Substituting g′ and f′ with the wrong sign, since they happen to both be positive here unlike g and f.
Sign slip turning −33 + 34 into −1 instead of 1.
steps.memory_tip: 2gg′ + 2ff′ = c + c′ is the ONE formula this whole chapter's VSAQ section tests — memorise it exactly as written, both sides.
